source.author: Jan-Cornelius Molnar

common_conventions.potential: Real-valued, mean-zero, period-one functions on T=R/Z. The same physical KdV Birkhoff map Omega is used in all statements.
common_conventions.coordinate_indices: n >= 1, with two real coordinates x_n,y_n; no n=0 action or signed duplicate
common_conventions.topologies: Sobolev and weighted Hilbert norm topologies; weighted actions use the indicated l1 norm. Bi-analyticity means real analytic maps with real analytic inverse in these norm topologies.
common_conventions.poisson: Gardner bracket integral (d_u F)*partial_x(d_u G); {x_n,y_m}=delta_nm, {x_n,x_m}={y_n,y_m}=0. This sign must not be inherited from the accepted NLS convention.
common_conventions.hill: L(q)=-d^2/dx^2+q on [0,2] with periodic boundary conditions, q period one. Fourier basis exp(i*pi*k*x); free spectral value pi^2*k^2. Formula (2), page 5, fixes the second derivative; the page-8 display has an omitted exponent.
common_conventions.spectral_labels: lambda_0^+, then pairs lambda_n^-,lambda_n^+ for n>=1, ordered lexicographically for complex q. Free n=0 is simple and n>=1 double; no perturbed multiplicity theorem is proved by the candidate.
common_conventions.contour_action: I_n=(1/pi) integral_Gamma_n lambda*Delta'(lambda)/sqrt_c(Delta(lambda)^2-4) d_lambda, with the branch/circuit conventions on pages 9-10. Higher actions J_(n,m) have lambda^(m+1)/((m+1)*pi).

main_statements.label: Theorem 1
main_statements.quantifier_order: Fix the same Omega; for every integer m>=1, there exist c_m>0,d_m>0, independent of u, such that for every u in H_0^m both estimates hold.
main_statements.adapter_constants: An action-bound constant C or D gives coordinate-bound constant 2*C or 2*D. These adapters require the physical identities and action bounds explicitly; they do not prove those hypotheses.

main_statements.label: Theorem 2
main_statements.quantifier_order: For every integer m>=1, there exist c_m>0,d_m>0 before quantifying every u in H_0^m.
main_statements.remaining: Construct physical Hill actions and hierarchy trace identities, complete global spectral/gap estimates, and prove the forward/inverse action bounds. The corrected-constant high-strip operator localization is now checked, but is not the theorem itself.

main_statements.label: Theorem 3
main_statements.domain: w_n=(1+|n|)^r*v_n, 0<=r<=1/2, v in M; H_0^w and h_*^w with weights w_(2*n), not w_n.
main_statements.weight_class: M: w_n>=1, w_(-n)=w_n, w_(n+k)<=w_n*w_k, and w_|n|<=w_(|n|+1). Piecewise linear interpolation to R is used in evaluating the bound.
main_statements.quantifier_order: For each admissible w,r there exists c_(w,r)>0 independent of u, then for every u in H_0^w, Omega(u) belongs to h_*^w and both estimates hold.
main_statements.remaining: Reuse SpectralWeight for M, prove the interpolation interface and weighted Hill gap/action estimates, then identify them with the physical Omega and its image space.

associated_corollaries.label: Corollary 1 (first occurrence)
associated_corollaries.scope: For integer m>=1, a global KdV solution with u(0)=u0 in H_0^m satisfies ||u(t)||_m<=alpha_m*(||u0||_m+(1+||u0||_(m-1))^(m^2+m-1)*||u0||_(m-1)) for every real t; alpha_m independent of u0,t.

associated_corollaries.label: Corollary 1 (second occurrence)
associated_corollaries.scope: For every real s>=0, exists c_s uniform in u in H_0^s: S_s<=c_s*(1+A_s)^max(1,s)*A_s and Q_(2*s+1)<=c_s^2*(1+A_s)^(2*max(1,s))*A_s^2, including the mapping property into h_*^s.

new_proved_foundation.source_correspondence: The free Fourier denominator and complementary inverse used in the proof of Lemma A.3, page 27, after the P_n/Q_n splitting on page 26. This is not Lemma A.3's full convolution estimate ||V*A_lambda^-1*Q_n||<=2*||q||_w/n.
new_proved_foundation.strip: For n>=1: |Re(lambda)-pi^2*n^2|<=6*n. This explicit narrower strip replaces the printed radius 12*n for this candidate; no downstream localization constants are yet claimed.
new_proved_foundation.domains_and_topologies: Complex Coeff p and WeightedCoeff w p, with 1<=p<=infinity and their Banach norms; arbitrary positive weight w. The reciprocal multiplier is zero when |k|=n and inverse(lambda-pi^2*k^2) otherwise.
new_proved_foundation.proved_bounds: |n^2-k^2|<=||lambda-pi^2*k^2|| for |k|!=n, and operator application norms <=(1/n)*||a|| for both unweighted and weighted spaces. The pointwise right inverse is the projection deleting the two resonant modes; uniqueness includes that deletion explicitly.
new_proved_foundation.not_claimed: No construction of perturbed Hill spectrum, periodic differential operator domain, discriminant, contour action, canonical coordinates or Birkhoff map. No result for the printed wider strips follows merely by renaming this strip.

continued_proved_foundation.source_correspondence: Lemma A.3, PDF/printed page 27, and the Neumann inversion at the start of page 28, on the explicit narrower radius-6*n strips.
proved: The actual complementary reciprocal symbol belongs to l2 with norm at most 4/n; this follows from the existing reciprocal series estimates via two translated punctured lattices.
hillComplementToL1 is a continuous linear map from weighted l2 to weighted l1 with the literal reciprocal coefficient formula and bound 4/n.
hillTailPerturbation is the literal weighted convolution q*(A_lambda^-1 Q_n a), with operator norm at most 4*||q||_w/n.
The l2-to-l1 and tail perturbation bounds hold uniformly for every integer shift of the weighted norm.

When n>=8*||q||_w, the tail operator has norm at most 1/2, and id minus that operator admits an actual two-sided bounded inverse of norm at most 2. The existence proof reuses NLS.exists_inverse_norm_le_two_mul_of_composition_near.
continued_proved_foundation.constant_changes: Uses 4/n for the summability and tail estimates, cutoff 8*||q||, and strip radius 6*n; no assertion of the printed 2/n estimate or radius 12*n follows.

two_mode_reduction.source_correspondence: Appendix A, page 28: S_n=A_lambda-P_n*T_hat_n*V, the one-to-one correspondence of nontrivial solutions, and the effective determinant criterion.
two_mode_reduction.statement: For a positive integer n, |Re(z)-pi^2*n^2|<=6*n, and n>=8*||q||_w, the determinant of the constructed operator on C x C vanishes iff there exists a nonzero weighted l1 sequence f with (z-pi^2*k^2)*f_k=(q*f)_k for every integer k. Reconstruction and resonant coefficient extraction recover the solutions in both directions. The full potential is the literal weighted convolution.
two_mode_reduction.free_case: At zero potential the constructed operator is (z-pi^2*n^2)*id, and its determinant is exactly (z-pi^2*n^2)^2.
two_mode_reduction.not_assumed: No unspecified finite block, arbitrary spectral package, or unproved inverse hypothesis is supplied by a caller. The bounded inverse is chosen from the previously proved existence theorem.
two_mode_reduction.remaining_qualifications: The physical H2 identification, joint analytic matching determinant, equal complex diagonal corrections, and shifted weighted coefficient bounds are proved. Agreement of determinant analytic orders with operator algebraic multiplicities and global eigenvalue labeling remain outstanding. The high-strip localization and two-analytic-zero count are recorded separately.

physical_hill_realization.source_correspondence: The periodic Hill operator -d^2/dx^2+q on [0,2], Section 2 page 8 and Appendix A pages 25-28. The domain is the periodic H2 space and the ambient physical space is complex L2 with normalized period-two Fourier coefficients.
physical_hill_realization.domain_description: WeightedCoeff (Weight.sobolev 2) 2, with its actual Hilbert norm. Its continuous physical representative F has a continuous periodic representative G of the first derivative; F and G are absolutely continuous on [0,2] and have square-integrable derivatives there. F prime equals G almost everywhere. Conversely every such physical periodic H2 function has a unique coefficient-domain representative.
physical_hill_realization.operator_description: The free part has symbol pi^2*k^2. It is the negative second derivative as a genuine tempered distribution. The potential term is the actual L2 product of the potential and the continuous H2 representative, by the existing physical convolution theorem. The physical output equals -G prime + q*F almost everywhere.
physical_hill_realization.eigenvector_regularization: Every unit-weight summable solution of the full Fourier eigen-equation automatically has Sobolev order two. The two-mode determinant therefore vanishes exactly when the constructed physical H2 Hill operator has a nonzero domain eigenvector on the stated strips and cutoff.
physical_hill_realization.scope_qualifications: The result works for arbitrary complex L2 potentials on the period-two circle. Source period-one/mean-zero potential restrictions still need their explicit application adapter. No compact resolvent, self-adjointness, eigenvalue labeling/counting/multiplicity, analytic determinant, or physical Birkhoff map is asserted by this milestone.

analytic_localization_zero_count.source_correspondence: Appendix A pages 27-29: analytic complementary inverse and effective determinant, the localization inclusion of Proposition A.1/Lemma A.5, and the two-root Rouche argument. These are proved for the explicit corrected strips/cutoffs below, and do not verify the global spectral enumeration or low central bounds of Proposition A.1.
analytic_localization_zero_count.analytic_scope: Joint complex Banach analyticity in the weighted l2 potential and spectral parameter at all points with |Re(z)-pi^2*n^2|<6*n and n>=8*||q||_w. The total determinant family is explicitly constructed, and equality with the original proof-indexed two-mode operator is proved. The inverse is constructed using Ring.inverse and its unit condition is derived from the checked tail bound.
analytic_localization_zero_count.localization_scope: For unit sequence weight, n>=1, |Re(z)-pi^2*n^2|<=6*n and n>=8*||q||, every effective determinant zero and every nonzero physical H2 eigenvector satisfies |z-pi^2*n^2|<=4*||q||. The proof uses the actual reconstructed correction and does not assume an eigenvalue estimate.
analytic_localization_zero_count.zero_count_scope: For n>=1 and n>=16*||q||, the actual determinant has analyticZeroCount=2 on the closed radius-n disc about pi^2*n^2. The quantitative bound |D(z)-(z-pi^2*n^2)^2|<=8*|z-pi^2*n^2|*||q||+32*||q||^2 proves the strict Rouche inequality. Localization proves the same count exhausts the whole closed radius-6*n real strip. This includes q=0 without a separate positive-norm assumption and allows colliding roots.
analytic_localization_zero_count.corrections: The complementary inverse strip remains radius 6*n. Localization uses cutoff 8*||q|| and bound 4*||q||. The two-zero count uses cutoff 16*||q|| and a radius-n counting circle. No assertion of the printed wider strip or printed cutoff follows by notation alone.
analytic_localization_zero_count.multiplicity_qualification: Analytic orders of this specific determinant are counted. Their equality with operator algebraic multiplicities, global periodic spectral labels, and the Hill discriminant zero orders remain outstanding.

weighted_effective_coefficients.source_correspondence: Appendix A page 28: equality a_n=a_-n and Lemma A.4. The estimates are pointwise uniformly throughout the explicit closed radius-6*n real strip, with cutoff n>=8*||q||_w.
weighted_effective_coefficients.proved: The tail inverse has norm at most two in every shifted weighted norm. Corrected unit-mode coefficients differ from the literal modulated potential by at most 8*||q||_w^2/n after multiplication by the appropriate shifted weight. In particular |a_n-q_0|<=8*||q||_w^2/n and w(2*n)*|c_+/-n-q_(+/-2*n)|<=8*||q||_w^2/n. The two diagonal terms agree for arbitrary complex potentials.
weighted_effective_coefficients.symmetry_proof: The actual reconstructed functions satisfy the full Fourier equation with exactly their resonant residual. The complex bilinear pairing sums a_k*b_-k without conjugation. Absolute convergence and convolution summation interchange reuse the verified coefficient-pairing library. The even free symbol gives the Green identity, which proves equality of the two diagonals without a reality or evenness hypothesis on q.
weighted_effective_coefficients.normalization_qualification: The raw period-two q_(+/-2*n) convention is converted by HillPeriodOnePotential to the exact source q_(+/-n) convention with the source norm w(2*n). The physical Fourier-integral equality is proved for every integrable period-one function carrying those coefficients.
weighted_effective_coefficients.remaining: No spectral gap bound or source main theorem is claimed by these coefficient estimates alone.

spectral_root_separation.source_correspondence: Appendix A pages 29-30: homogeneous-diagonal determinant factorization and the root-separation step in Lemma A.6/Proposition A.7, with corrected strip/cutoff/constants.
spectral_root_separation.spectral_variation: For any z,y in the closed radius-6*n real strip, the diagonal difference is at most (16*||q||_w^2/n^2)*|z-y|. At cutoff n>=8*||q||_w this is at most |z-y|/4. The proof uses the literal complementary resolvent identity, a proved inverse-difference identity, and shifted norms; it does not assume a Cauchy derivative estimate.
spectral_root_separation.factorization: The constructed operator sends u to ((z-sigma_n-a_n)*u_1-c_n*u_2,(z-sigma_n-a_n)*u_2-c_-n*u_1), and its actual analytic determinant equals (z-sigma_n-a_n)^2-c_n*c_-n.
spectral_root_separation.root_separation: For n>=1, n>=8*||q||_w and any two zeros z,y of the constructed determinant in the stated strip: w(2*n)^2*|z-y|^2 <= 9*w(2*n)^2*(|q_(2*n)|^2+|q_(-2*n)|^2)+1152*||q||_w^4/n^2. Coincident roots are allowed.
spectral_root_separation.reuse: The product determinant formula and quantitative determinant-shift bound previously private to HillZeroCount have been moved to a single shared two-dimensional determinant module, generalized to any nontrivially normed field and reused by both Hill consumers.
spectral_root_separation.remaining_qualifications: The bound concerns actual determinant zeros. The exact source period-one coefficient/norm adapter and summed tail estimate are now supplied. Global periodic eigenvalue labels and equality of determinant orders and operator multiplicities remain open. Main Theorems 1-3 remain unverified.

period_one_weighted_gap_tail.source_correspondence: Appendix A page 30 Proposition A.7, with the exact period-one coefficient convention and corrected cutoff/quartic constant. The Sobolev norm adapter matches the main Theorems 1-2 norms on page 3; the weight adapter matches Theorem 3 on page 4.
period_one_weighted_gap_tail.norm_and_potential_identification: Pullback of a positive weight along an integer embedding makes actual zero insertion an isometry. The target period-two weight w pulls back to the source weight k -> w(2*k), still in the source spectral-weight class. The raw even coefficient equals q_k, every odd coefficient vanishes, the mean coefficient and Fourier reality are preserved, and forgetting the weight gives the existing Coeff.periodDouble. For an integrable physical period-one function with those original coefficients, the embedded sequence equals its actual period-two Fourier integrals.
period_one_weighted_gap_tail.sobolev_normalization: For each natural m, the squared weighted norm is exactly sum over k in Z of (1+|2*pi*k|)^(2*m)*|q_k|^2, proved as a HasSum statement. No equivalent-norm substitution is used.
period_one_weighted_gap_tail.individual_gap: For n>=1, n>=8*||q||_w and any two zeros in the stated high strip, w(2*n)*|xi_plus-xi_minus|<=6*||q||_w.
period_one_weighted_gap_tail.summed_gap: For N>=1 and N>=8*||q||_w, any actual determinant-root families lying in their respective high strips have summable squared weighted differences and sum_{n>=N} w(2*n)^2*|xi_plus_n-xi_minus_n|^2 <= 9*||R_N q||_w^2+(2304/N)*||q||_w^4. The source tail is represented by Coeff.fourierTail N applied to the actual weighted source coefficients, retaining the boundary |k|=N.
period_one_weighted_gap_tail.constant_corrections: Retains source individual constant 6 and coefficient-tail factor 9, with cutoff 8*||q||_w, radius-6*n real strips, and quartic coefficient 2304 replacing the printed 576. These follow from the previously corrected inverse bound 4/n rather than the printed 2/n.
period_one_weighted_gap_tail.qualifications: The root hypotheses concern the constructed analytic determinant, not freely supplied spectral data. Global eigenvalue labels, their agreement with these root families, operator algebraic multiplicities and the low central estimates remain unproved. The statements do not claim Theorems 1-3.

classical_discriminant_reuse.actual_construction: The imported constant-upper state map is proved to turn actual constructed ZS IVP solutions for (-1,-q) into scalar Hill solutions of -F second+q*F=lambda*F, with bijective position/derivative initial state, including lambda=0. Even descent through the spectral square proves joint complex Banach analyticity of the literal normalized scalar trace in energy and the continuous potential with its sup norm.
classical_discriminant_reuse.new_comparison: A direct scalar Volterra state flow for (F,G) prime=(G,(q-lambda)*F) is constructed and proved identical to that shared scalar IVP, with its exact trace equal to classicalHillDiscriminant. Absolute-continuity uniqueness identifies every scalar weak solution with the same actual initial state. For a continuous physical circle potential Q, every eigenvector of this branch’s actual periodic H2 Hill operator has this scalar state flow on [0,1], with F its continuous representative and G its actual continuous derivative representative.
classical_discriminant_reuse.source_correspondence: Section 2 pages 8-10: physical Hill discriminant and scalar solutions. This is the continuous-potential discriminant and weak-to-classical IVP comparison, not yet the global product/action construction.
classical_discriminant_reuse.qualifications: The H2 comparison is proved on the unit interval. The full period-two endpoint comparison, periodic/antiperiodic characteristic equivalence with the Fourier determinant, equality of zero orders/multiplicities, global labels and L2-potential extension remain open. The source Theorem 3 includes L2 inputs, so the continuous-potential result cannot silently replace that domain.
